scenario: Explicit immutable write-job catalogs and bounded read-only current observations

stages.label: explicit-membership-freezes-order
stages.explanation: A catalog explicitly pins long then minimum; its actual discarded create response is recovered by exact replay, and bounded pages preserve order and terminal emptiness.

stages.label: later-job-needs-an-explicit-new-catalog
stages.explanation: A later prepared job is not automatically added to the first catalog. The second pins long, late and minimum from intent metadata even while the late target is unavailable; pages retain that row and recover after the target returns.

stages.label: pages-observe-phases-without-advancing
stages.explanation: Only ordinary write steps advance the later job through ready, linked and completed. Catalog pages retain the same descriptor and show each current status without changing controls; compatible review and separate revalidation remain advisory.

stages.label: unavailable-and-changed-members-stay-visible
stages.explanation: An absent job retains one unavailable row. Swapping two existing completed job directories retains two changed rows before intent parsing; restoring paths restores ordinary observations and every historical descriptor remains fixed.

stages.label: historical-catalog-survives-input-loss
stages.explanation: With twenty explicit paths absent, both shows and exact create replay remain historical and pages retain unavailable member rows. After the six job/target paths return, pages observe all jobs while fourteen original source paths are still absent; every path returns in finally.

stages.label: catalogs-do-not-authorize-domain-actions
stages.explanation: Invalid cursors and different ordered requests refuse safely. Final catalogs, completed writes, previous reviews, case catalogs, case details and blocked jobs preserve their histories; no catalog page advances a job or grants authority.

limits: Membership is an explicit ordered selection; later jobs are not discovered or added automatically. Two catalogs preserve different compositions and identities.

Catalog capture reads validated immutable write intents without target status. A target may be unavailable during capture; a later page retains its descriptor beside an unavailable current observation.

Pages retain compact seven-field historical descriptors beside validated full current status or a fixed changed/unavailable observation. Changed pins are detected before parsing the replacement intent.
Only ordinary write steps advance the later job. Catalog show, replay and pages do not acquire work leases, advance jobs, revalidate original source inputs or grant domain authorization.
The cursor fixes catalog identity and position, not a common state snapshot. checked_at dates one sequential page pass; current job phases may differ on later pages.
An actual validated create reply is discarded and recovered by exact replay. Its ephemeral comparison digest is not exported.

Twenty paths are temporarily absent; job and target paths are then restored while fourteen original source paths remain unavailable. Every path returns in finally, and blocked restore jobs never move.
Static directory identities and full file metadata are compared; directory times changed by rename are excluded. Public Store comparison excludes only top-level governance observed_at.

Actors remain self-declared. Available/current/completed and a matching separate basis do not establish authentication, independent expertise, semantic truth, archival, deletion or activation of old authority.
No new fault worker, forced interruption, partial control write, storage failure, workload capacity or process-overlap measurement is introduced.
